headline: The midday models roughly doubled tonight's rain, with HRRR and ECMWF now near 0.27 in in the wettest 3 hours centered on the 1 AM high tide; the rating card is still none, but a heavier shower could briefly flood gutters and low spots.

summary.text: Up since this morning: HRRR 0.12 to 0.27 in, RRFS 0.07 to 0.15 in, ECMWF 0.12 to 0.27 in for the wettest 3 hours. HRRR's peak hour jumped from 0.09 to 0.24 in.
Wettest 3 hours: ECMWF 0.27, HRRR 0.27 (GFS copies it), RRFS 0.15, NBM 0.07 in. Storm totals 0.09 to 0.37 in. NBM is the low outlier; all agree on one quick overnight band.
Rating card consensus 0.15 in: none. Likely too low given HRRR's under-forecast history; a heavier cell could reach sidewalk level. Yellow (garage) needs about 0.71 in in 3 hours or a 0.40 in hour.
Light rain from about 10 to 11 PM, heaviest roughly 1 to 3 AM Wednesday, showers ending by mid-morning. Thanksgiving and Friday dry; light rain possible Sunday, wetter around next Tuesday.
The burst lands on the 7.1 ft high at 1:12 AM, running about 8.5 ft with surge, so the channel drains slowly until about 3 to 4 AM. Channel low: 0.13 ft at 1 PM.
Before dark: clear street drain grates and yard drains. If a downpour hits around 1 to 3 AM, move cars out of the cul-de-sac. Stay off the Bay shore at the late-morning king tides.

sections.title: Synopsis
sections.text: A cold front is moving into the region from the northwest: clouds are increasing and showers were developing on the Sonoma coast early this afternoon. NWS San Francisco (short and long term issued 12:00 PM) has the main front crossing tonight, with south gusts of 25 to 35 mph for coastal and bay shore areas this evening (down from about 40 mph in the morning discussion) and most of the rain overnight. The band weakens as it moves south, breaking into scattered showers by the Wednesday commute and ending by afternoon. NWS rain totals: 0.25 to 0.50 in for San Francisco and the bay shore, 0.5 to 0.75 in on the Peninsula's coastal slopes, under 0.25 in for the South Bay. Weak instability over the coastal waters gives a 15 percent chance of a few heavier showers or a thunderstorm north of Santa Cruz; NWS notes that both HRRR and RRFS show localized rates over 0.50 in per hour, with HRRR hinting at a shower near 1 in per hour, and that heavier downpours could cause localized flooding. Thanksgiving and Friday dry and near average; light rain likely Sunday, with a stronger trough possible around next Tuesday. The Coastal Flood Warning for the San Francisco and San Pablo Bay shorelines continues until 4 PM Thursday.

sections.title: What changed and model trends
sections.text:
Since this morning's discussion every model except NBM has come up, and the rain is now concentrated earlier, around 1 to 3 AM instead of 3 to 5 AM in HRRR. Two models (HRRR and ECMWF) now cross 0.25 in in 3 hours, which puts tonight on the storm horizon even though it stays far below the flooding thresholds.

Wettest 3 hours / storm total, 1 PM Tuesday onward (72 hours):
• HRRR (11 AM Tue run, out to 10 AM Thu): 0.27 / 0.32 in, about 0.02 in per hour from 10 PM, then 0.24 in in the hour around 2 AM, a small shower near 6 AM. Up from 0.12 / 0.12 in; peak hour up from 0.09 in.
• HRRR 15-minute (ends 11:45 PM Wednesday): sprinkles from about 10 PM, then 0.059 and 0.075 in in back-to-back 15 minutes around 2 AM (a rate near 0.3 in per hour), light showers again 5 to 6 AM.
• RRFS (4 AM Tue run): 0.15 / 0.15 in, almost all of it (0.12 in) in the hour around 2 AM. Up from 0.07 / 0.07 in.
• NBM: 0.07 / 0.09 in, about 1 to 5 AM. Little changed from 0.06 / 0.06 in.
• ECMWF: 0.27 / 0.37 in, the wettest total: about 0.02 in per hour from 10 PM, then 0.09 in per hour for three hours around 1 to 4 AM, a few hundredths into Wednesday midday. Up from 0.12 / 0.23 in.
• GFS: identical to HRRR hour for hour again, so no independent information.

The 2 AM burst in HRRR is supported by RRFS (same hour) and ECMWF (same window), so it is not an isolated shower cell.

Consensus (HRRR 0.27 × 1.25 = 0.34, RRFS 0.15, NBM 0.07): middle value 0.15 in, up from 0.07 in. The rating card stays at none. I think that is on the low side tonight: HRRR has under-forecast big local bursts here by about 3×, and three times its 3-hour amount (about 0.8 in) or its peak hour (about 0.7 in) would reach Yellow. That is the worst case, not the expected case; the most likely outcome is a quarter inch or so with gutters running full for an hour.

sections.title: Tide and the channel
sections.text:
NOAA's Bay model (run now ends 7 AM Thursday) runs about 1.1 to 1.4 ft above the predicted tides at Redwood City. This evening's -1.5 ft low at 6:28 PM runs about -0.3 ft near 7:20 PM, a good window for the channel to drain before the rain.

The heaviest rain now lands right on the 7.1 ft high at 1:12 AM Wednesday: the model has 7.3 ft at midnight, 8.3 ft at 1 AM, a crest near 8.5 ft at 1:30 AM, 8.5 ft at 2 AM, 7.7 ft at 3 AM and 6.5 ft at 4 AM. All four independent models put their wettest hour within that high, so the channel and the street drains empty slowly during the burst and drain better after about 3 to 4 AM. The 3.2 ft low at 6:14 AM runs about 4.3 ft. Wednesday's 9.5 ft king tide at 11:46 AM runs about 11.0 ft near noon, after the rain has ended. (This morning's 9.5 ft king tide ran about 10.9 ft.)

NWS: at the San Francisco gauge, highs 2.7 ft above normal Wednesday (8.5 ft at 10:49 AM), 2.2 ft Thursday and 2.0 ft Friday and Saturday, including up to 1.6 ft of surge, approaching the highest tide ever recorded there.

Channel: at Alameda de las Pulgas 0.13 ft at 1 PM, flat between 0.12 and 0.15 ft for 24 hours (Flood Monitoring 3.18 ft). Upstream of Caltrain: 0.07 ft at 5:13 AM, still its latest report (Flood Monitoring 2.8 ft).

sections.title: Current observations
sections.text: Dry on the street, with clouds thickening and south winds increasing. The Caltrain rain gauge has not reported since 5:13 AM (no rain in the 24 hours to then). NWS satellite shows a 200 to 300 mile cloud field with the front, and showers starting along the Sonoma coast.

sections.title: Uncertainty
sections.text: Moderate. The models agree well on timing (one band, heaviest around 1 to 3 AM) and on a storm total under 0.4 in, but differ by about 4× on the burst (NBM 0.07 in vs HRRR and ECMWF 0.27 in for 3 hours). The front is forecast to weaken as it reaches the South Bay, which favors the lower numbers; the convective showers NWS mentions favor the higher ones, and a single heavy shower overhead could briefly exceed every model. The burst coinciding with the 1 AM high tide is the main aggravating factor for the channel. RRFS is from an older 4 AM run; the next RRFS and HRRR runs will show whether the burst holds.

sections.title: What to do
sections.text:
• Before dark today: clear leaves from street drain grates and yard drains; secure loose items for the evening wind.
• Tonight: no need to move cars on current guidance, but if rain turns heavy around 1 to 3 AM, move them out of the cul-de-sac and take timestamped photos of the street at the peak.
• Gusts of 25 to 35 mph this evening can still cause outages that slow the pumps.
• Keep this page open overnight if you're up; check the next update around midnight.
• Stay away from the Bay shore, tidal sloughs and low shoreline roads at the late-morning king tides Wednesday and Thursday; don't walk or drive through moving water.
